source: Wikipedia, National debt of the United States
what: highlight "surpassed $40 trillion on August 18, 2026"
said: On August eighteenth, twenty twenty-six, America's national debt passed forty trillion dollars.

source: Wikipedia, National debt of the United States
what: highlight "a time interval of merely 71 days"
said: Less than a year earlier, it had just hit thirty-eight trillion. And the jump from thirty-seven to thirty-eight took only seventy-one days.

source: U.S. Treasury, Fiscal Data
what: highlight "The national debt is the amount of money the federal government has borrowed"
said: First, what is the national debt? It is every dollar the federal government has borrowed and not yet paid back.

source: U.S. Treasury, Fiscal Data
what: highlight "similar to a person using a credit card"
said: The Treasury itself explains it with a simple picture. It is like using a credit card and never paying off the full balance.

source: U.S. Treasury, Fiscal Data
what: highlight "Debts incurred during the American Revolutionary War amounted to $75 million"
said: America has carried debt since the very beginning. The Revolutionary War left the new country owing seventy-five million dollars, much of it borrowed from France.

source: U.S. Treasury, Fiscal Data
what: highlight "As the federal government experiences reoccurring deficits, which is common, the national debt grows."
said: Every year the government spends more than it collects in taxes. That gap is called the deficit. Each deficit gets added to the pile.

source: Wikipedia, National debt of the United States
what: highlight "$26.5 trillion held by the public and $12.1 trillion in intragovernmental debt"
said: At the end of twenty twenty-three, about twenty-six and a half trillion was held by the public, and about twelve trillion was owed inside the government.

source: Wikipedia, National debt of the United States
what: highlight "reached its highest level during Harry Truman 's first presidential term"
said: When the war ended, America owed more than its entire economy produced in a year.

source: Wikipedia, National debt of the United States
what: highlight "debt-to-GDP ratio fell from 1.21 to 0.32"
said: Now here is the amazing part. By nineteen seventy-four, that number had fallen to just thirty-two percent.

source: Wikipedia, National debt of the United States
what: highlight "there were surpluses in only eight of those years"
said: In those twenty-eight years, the government ran a surplus in only eight of them. A surplus is a year when it collects more than it spends.

source: Wikipedia, National debt of the United States
what: highlight "reached a low in 1974 under president Richard Nixon"
said: The debt hit its lowest point compared to the economy under President Nixon, in nineteen seventy-four.

source: Wikipedia, History of the Federal Reserve System
what: highlight "pledged to keep the interest rate on Treasury bills fixed at 0.375 percent"
said: During the war, the Federal Reserve promised to keep the rate on short-term government debt fixed at just three eighths of one percent.

source: Wikipedia, Financial repression
what: highlight "negative real interest rates erodes the real value of government debt"
said: Economists have a name for this mix. They call it financial repression. Rates are held below inflation, so savers slowly lose value without noticing.

source: Wikipedia, Financial repression
what: highlight "below 1% for two-thirds of the time between 1945 and 1980"
said: After the war, America kept real interest rates below one percent for two thirds of the time between nineteen forty-five and nineteen eighty.

source: Wikipedia, Financial repression
what: highlight "inflate away"
said: That is how the country was able to inflate away the giant debt left by the Depression and the war.

source: Wikipedia, Financial repression
what: highlight "government debt declined from 216% of GDP in 1945 to 138% ten years later in 1955"
said: And America was not alone. Britain used the same trick. Its debt fell from two hundred sixteen percent of its economy to one hundred thirty-eight percent in just ten years.

source: Wikipedia, Financial repression
what: highlight "financial repression can last for decades"
said: And this is not a quick trick. Research on Japan suggests it can go on for decades.

source: Wikipedia, Financial repression
what: highlight "can be considered a form of taxation"
said: That is why economists say financial repression works like a hidden tax. It moves wealth from savers to the borrower.

source: Wikipedia, 2021–2023 inflation surge
what: highlight "By June 2022, inflation in the US peaked at 9.1%, a record not seen since 1981."
said: We got a taste of this recently. In June twenty twenty-two, American inflation hit nine point one percent, the highest in about forty years.

source: Wikipedia, 2021–2023 inflation surge
what: highlight "Fuel prices rose by 49% from January to June 2022 in the United States."
said: At the same time, the debt shrank a little compared to the economy, because prices and incomes in dollars were suddenly much bigger.

source: Wikipedia, History of the Federal Reserve System
what: highlight "restored independence to the Fed"
said: It was called the Accord, and it gave the Federal Reserve back its independence. The Fed could now raise rates when it wanted to fight inflation.

source: Wikipedia, National debt of the United States
what: highlight "federal interest payments on the national debt surpassed spending on both Medicare and national defense"
said: The second problem is interest. In twenty twenty-four, interest payments on the debt grew bigger than spending on Medicare and on the military.

source: Wikipedia, National debt of the United States
what: highlight "to $799 billion in 2024, or 3.0% of GDP"
said: Just ten years earlier, net interest was about two hundred thirty-one billion dollars a year. By twenty twenty-four, it was almost eight hundred billion.

source: Wikipedia, National debt of the United States
what: highlight "to 116 percent in 2034"
said: Its forecast says debt held by the public goes from ninety-nine percent of the economy in twenty twenty-four to one hundred sixteen percent in twenty thirty-four.

source: Wikipedia, National debt of the United States
what: highlight "172 percent of GDP in 2054"
said: If nothing changes, the same forecast keeps climbing, to one hundred seventy-two percent of the economy by twenty fifty-four. That is far above the World War Two record.
